terms.meaning: Rule of the people. From Greek "Demos" (people) and "Kratia" (rule).
People themselves make policies and laws. Works only in small countries, such as Switzerland.
People elect representatives who make the laws. It suits big countries like India.
The right of every adult to vote, whatever their caste, religion, language or gender.
An election to fill a seat that falls vacant within the five-year term.

items.name: Democracy in ancient India
items.formula: The Sabha and Samithi of the Vedic period.
items.example: It works on "one man, one vote".

items.name: Abraham Lincoln's definition
items.formula: Government of the people, by the people and for the people.
items.example: He was a President of the USA.

items.name: Lord Bryce's definition
items.formula: Power lies with the whole community, not with any one class.

items.name: Herman Finer's definition
items.formula: Democracy is not only a form of government but also a way of life.
items.example: It stresses daily life, not just elections.

items.name: Tools of direct democracy
items.example: It was practised in ancient Greece.

items.name: Main features of democracy
items.formula: Consent of the people, free and fair elections at intervals, rule of law, rights, and a recognised opposition.
items.example: Liberty and equality are its basis; it is against personality worship.

items.name: What democracy needs to succeed
items.formula: Alert people, tolerance, good leaders, a strong opposition, educated voters and a free press.
items.example: Efficient local bodies strengthen it too.

items.name: Merits of democracy
items.formula: Equality, decisions by debate, rights through an independent judiciary, peaceful change of government.
items.example: It lowers the danger of revolution.

items.name: A demerit of democracy
items.formula: Representatives without education, skill or leadership, or with selfish aims, weaken it.
items.example: Ignorance of social and economic issues does harm.

items.name: Voting age in India
items.formula: 18 years, lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment of 1989.
items.example: Someone born in 2008 could vote in 2026.

items.name: What to look for in a candidate
items.formula: Keen to serve, approachable, educated and honest, not corrupt, with no criminal record.
items.example: Voters must not be swayed by caste, money or muscle power.

items.name: General elections
items.formula: Held every five years in India.

items.name: Election Commission of India
items.formula: One Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, appointed by the President; based in New Delhi.
items.example: State Election Commissions hold local body elections.

mistakes.text: India is too large for direct democracy, so it has representative democracy. Switzerland has direct democracy.
The voting age became 18 through the 61st Amendment; the 42nd Amendment added fundamental duties.
A by-election fills one vacant seat mid-term; a general election is held for all seats every five years.
